hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $1 + 3^2$ first. The power comes before the adding, so it is $1 + 9 = 10$. This problem starts the same way.
Look for the exponent. Powers are worked out before any adding or subtracting.
Replace $2^3$ with $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$. The expression becomes $5 + 8 - 4$, which you work from left to right.

explanation: Exponents come before addition and subtraction, so find $2^3$ first: $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$.
Put that value back in, which turns the expression into $5 + 8 - 4$.
Addition and subtraction go left to right, so add first: $5 + 8 = 13$.
Then subtract: $13 - 4 = 9$. The value of the expression is $9$.
